answer: Sybil farms often share one machine, so their response timing gives them away. A verifier sends each agent a burst of probes, a small gale of requests, and records the latency curve. Like light through a prism, that curve splits into distinct signatures: independent agents scatter, while a hundred fake identities on one host return nearly identical profiles. The network groups matching fingerprints and pays the cluster a single share. Honest agents feel only a velvet touch, a few milliseconds of probing per epoch.
